Add a CI gate for pull request texts (#268)

Add tools/check-pr-text.py, a gate that checks a pull request
description and its committed squash-message file,
.github/squash/<number>.txt. In both texts it checks review-history
labels, through the label lint loaded by file path, em and en dashes,
-ise spellings whose -ize form is the standard one, an empty or blank
text, and a code fence that is opened and never closed. A blank text
holds nothing once whitespace, zero-width spaces, byte order marks and
HTML comments are removed. In the squash message it also checks line
width, revision ids and a subject that ends with the pull request
number. Fenced code, inline code, URLs and the text on 1 line between
a pair of straight double quote marks, or between U+201C and the next
U+201D, are masked from the label, dash and spelling checks; a mixed
or reversed pair is not masked. A fence closes only on a closer
followed by nothing but spaces or tabs; a fence that is never closed
masks the rest of the text and is reported at its opener. A URL ends
before whitespace, an angle bracket, a straight or curly quote mark,
a backtick, an em or en dash, an unpaired parenthesis or trailing
punctuation, and the width check skips fenced code and a line whose
excess lies in 1 URL that reaches its end. The gate finds the lint
and the squash folder from its own path and makes no git call. For
the inputs it reads, it exits 2 on unreadable input, on any other
exception raised while it runs, an interrupt among them, and on a
usage error, with the defect count as its last line. Its inline-code
scan takes time linear in the length of a line. Add its suite,
tools/test-check-pr-text.py, with a mutant sweep that records a
failing case for each guard it lists, and the workflow
.github/workflows/pr-text.yml, which runs the gate on every pull
request with read-only permissions, keeps no credentials after
checkout and stops the job after 10 minutes. tools/ci-status.py does
not insist on the new check. tools/run_all_checks.sh runs the gate's
suite, and tools/test-run-all-checks.py lists the workflow's event step
as an exception, with the suite in its place.

Residuals: a defect in a form the patterns miss, such as an upper-case
revision id, an -ise stem the denylist lacks, or a listed stem with a
prefix such as re- or un- or a further suffix such as -isational; a
defect inside a masked region, such as an em dash inside double
quotes, between 2 inch marks or in the lines that an unclosed fence
masks, or in a region the gate masks but a renderer shows as prose,
such as a fence inside an HTML block or a span opened by a backtick
escaped with a backslash; a false failure on honest text, such as code
in an indented block, a list item or a blockquote, a code span or a
quotation that wraps a line, a URL in angle brackets or backticks or
followed by punctuation that runs past 72 characters, a line that
combining marks push past 72 code points, a hex run with digits and
letters in a squash message, or a bare id of 1 or 2 capital letters
and 1 or 2 digits; a lint that ends the gate process, writes to
standard output or closes it, since the lint is trusted repository
code run in that process, a standard output that cannot be written,
or an input that never ends, such as a FIFO, or a payload nested so
deeply that, on a stack with no limit, its parse uses up memory, any
of which can end the gate with another status, with no count line or
with a line that has no prefix; a message typed into the merge dialog
that differs from the committed file; and a description edited after
the last run.
